summary: Report the projection comparison made at the last aligned exchange, so same-build pairs stop reading waiting, and name why a pair waits

replay.detail: No claim replay or recovery behavior changes; only the replication status derives its comparison fields differently.

schema.detail: No tables, indexes, triggers, schema-version changes or data rewrites. The held comparison lives in memory beside the existing per-peer sync measurements and is rebuilt by the first aligned exchange after a restart. A comparison that found every projection equal is reported for up to five minutes while inventories move, so an equal result can be that old; the status says when it was made.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or digest changes; no coordinated member upgrade required.

compatibility.detail: Replication status gains three optional peer fields: projection_comparison_waiting_reason, projection_graphs_equal and projection_compared_at_unix_ms. Older clients ignore them, and a newer client reading an older daemon falls back to comparing digests as before.

downtime.detail: No additional startup work or expected interruption.

manual.detail: No operator actions, client re-pairing or configuration changes required.

recovery.detail: No persistent state changes or new swap-back restrictions.
